title: Assembly and Tracking of Microbial Community Development within a Microwell Array Platform
protocol: Deposit between 1-1.5 µm of parylene N on silicon wafers using a commercially available system.
Spin-coat the parylene N-coated wafers with adhesion promoter at 3,000 rpm for 45 s.
Sprinkle adhesion promoter over the entire wafer and let sit for approximately 10 s before spinning dry.
Dispense positive-tone photoresist in the center of the wafer and spin at 3,000 rpm for 45 s to yield a resist coating that is approximately 1.5 µm thick.
Soft-bake the samples on a hotplate at 115 °C for 1 min.
Use a contact aligner and photomask with the desired well pattern to expose the sample to ultraviolet light.
Expose the spin-coated wafer through the patterned photomask for 6 s.
Submerge the sample in developer containing less than 3% tetramethyl ammonium hydroxide in water for 2 minutes.
Rinse the sample with deionized water.
Dry the sample with clean, dry nitrogen.
Use an oxygen plasma etch at 60 mTorr, 20 °C, 100 sccm O2, and 10 W RF, 2,000 W ICP to remove exposed parylene down to the silicon substrate.
Load the sample into a physical profilometer.
Turn on the sample vacuum.
Press the manual load button.
Focus the system onto the sample by pressing the "Focus" button.
Position an appropriate feature for measurement on the view screen.
Scan the sample.
Level the profile and measure the feature depth.
Record the etch rate and modulate subsequent etch times to achieve the desired depth.
Start colonies on Luria Broth (LB) agar plates from glycerol stocks.
Pick colonies of the desired strains from LB agar plates.
Start overnight cultures of P. aeruginosa in R2A medium.
Incubate the overnight cultures for approximately 18 h at 37 °C while shaking at 220 rpm.
Use a diamond scribe to section the silicon wafer into individual chips containing the ensembles of different sizes and pitch-well arrays.
Ensure that each chip contains the full complement of well sizes and pitches for the study.
Place a 150 µL droplet of 500 µg/mL Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) in PBS on top of the array.
Incubate the BSA solution for 1 h at room temperature in a humid chamber.
Remove the BSA solution after incubation.
Rinse the array with PBS three times by removing and replacing the liquid droplet.
Dry the array under nitrogen.
Add 150 µL of 0.02 OD cultures to each dry array placed in a humid chamber.
Incubate for 1 h at 4 °C to allow bacteria to adhere to well walls.
Turn on the stage-top environmental control chamber.
Adjust settings on the control box for humidity and temperature equilibration before adding samples.
Level the sample holder using a bubble level.
Line the interior around the sample with PBS-soaked lab wipes to increase humidity in the chamber.
Set the temperature of the chamber to 30 °C and that of the lid to 32 °C to reduce condensation on the imaging plane.
Manually turn on the power switch for the mercury lamp at least 30 min prior to imaging.
Manually turn on the camera and automated microscope stage.
Open the software used to control the microscope and peripheral equipment.
Ensure that the equipment is recognized by the software.
Microwave previously prepared agarose solutions until a liquid state is reached, approximately 60 s.
Wet the back of a 75 mm x 22 mm, #1.5 glass coverslip with ethanol.
Place the wetted coverslip lengthwise and centered across a 2 x 3" glass slide.
Place two PDMS spacers along the long edges of the coverslip.
Shift the glass coverslip so that roughly 1 mm is overhanging the edge of the slide.
Pour 5 mL of liquid agarose solution on top of the glass coverslip to completely cover it.
Place a second 2 x 3" glass slide on top of the assembly to sandwich the liquid agar between the coverslip and slide.
Allow the glass slide-coverslip-agarose gel-glass slide sandwich to set until the agarose begins to solidify.
Transfer the sandwich to a refrigerator for 15 minutes.
Remove excess solidified agarose and cut around the glass coverslip.
Move the prepared coverslip to a clean dish and place it in a refrigerator until use.
Dip silicon chips individually in ultrapure water, each for 10 seconds.
Set the chips on their edges until most of the liquid has drained.
Cut tape pieces matching the edge length of the silicon chips.
Place tape on the parylene covering the silicon chip.
Quickly peel away the parylene coating using the tape.
Invert each peeled chip and place it such that its microwell-array side contacts the agarose-coated side of the coverslip.
Avoid moving or shifting the chip after contact to prevent bacterial growth outside the wells.
Place the assembled microwell array/agarose coverslip in the slide holder of the stage-top environmental control chamber on the microscope.
Use ambient light or directed light to locate arrays of interest.
Turn off ambient or directed light after storing positions.
Open the "ND Acquisition" panel in commercial software.
Click on the "XY menu" and check an empty box for each position that needs to be saved.
Click on the "Include Z" button.
Acquire images over time at desired wavelengths using fluorescence filter cubes.
Move to each saved location using control software.
Focus on the wells using the GFP filter.
Adjust focus and save new z-position by clicking the arrow pointing at the z-location.
Determine the z-axis distance between focal planes for each wavelength by noting the difference in the z-axis position when focused on the surface of the array.
Choose 2-3 locations from the array with the mixed red/green bacteria population and focus using the Red Fluorescence Protein (RFP) filter.
Subtract the distance between the focal planes using the GFP and RFP fluorescence filters and add that focal plane adjustment under the "λ" menu.
Begin time-lapse image acquisition.
Set the "interval" to 30 min and the "duration of the experiment" to 24 h under the "Time" menu.
With the "Time," "XY," and "λ" boxes checked, run the program.
Move the stage to image each location.
Take an image in one wavelength.
Adjust z-position for focal plane differences.
Take a second image at adjusted z-position.
Proceed to the next array location (multipoint).
Loop through all locations at 30 min intervals (time-lapse).
Acquire illumination control images using "ND Acquisition," "Time," and "XY" menus.
Capture 100 darkfield images with all light sources off.
Use longest exposure time from timelapse for darkfield images.
Take 100 illumination field images of a standard slide at different locations.
Choose an exposure time to maximize signal without saturation.
Convert acquired images to tiff file format using commercial software.
Upload images into image analysis software by clicking "File">"Import">"Image Sequence."
Create a "Correction Image" by averaging all "darkfield" and "illumination field" images.
Load the average "darkfield" image and the average "illumination field" image.
Subtract the average "darkfield" image from the average "illumination field" image using "Process" > "Image Calculator."
Select "Image1" as the darkfield image and "Image2" as the illumination field image in the Image Calculator.
Choose "Subtract" in the "Operation" field of the Image Calculator.
Click "OK" to create the correction image.
Load the correction images, then click "Image" > "Stacks" > "Z Project."
Select "Average Projection" for averaging the stack.
Perform background subtraction by clicking "Process" > "Subtract Background."
Enter a radius (e.g., 125) in the "radius" field and select "sliding paraboloid."
Click "OK" to apply the background subtraction.
Perform illumination correction using "Process" > "Calculator Plus."
Choose operation as "divide," i1 as well image, i2 as correction image, k1 as correction image mean, and k2 as 0.
Click "Create New Window" to perform the division operation.
Select regions of interest (ROIs) around each microwell in the desired arrays using the ImageJ "MicroArray" plugin.
In the "MAP" menu, click "Reset Grid."
Specify rows, columns, and diameter based on well size and number on the array.
Select "circle" from the "ROI shape" menu.
Hold the "Alt" key while selecting the top-left ROI with the mouse to move the ROI array.
Hold the "shift" key while selecting the bottom-left ROI to change the size of the array.
Hold the "shift" key while selecting an ROI from the right side of the array, but not at the corners, to change the spacing of the ROIs.
Fit the ROI array over the wells in an image.
Click "Measure RT."
Use three ROI sizes to create concentric rings around the wells for collecting local background signal and fluorescence measurements.
Collect data in a spreadsheet software and calculate the background signal.
Import collected data into a custom scripting software for further analysis.
Organize the data collected in ImageJ into a matrix with columns for sub-array number, well row, well column, mean intensity, background intensity, and mean intensity minus background intensity.
Separate the results of the mCherry and GFP acquisition into different matrices.
Store the results from each sub-array in a different cell in a cell array.
Store the results from each color in a different cell in a cell array.
Adjust for the autofluorescence of P. aeruginosa.
Analyze an mCherry-only chip to ascertain the relationship between mCherry and green autofluorescence.
Plot the mCherry-versus-GFP signal from all mCherry ΔretSΔtse/i1-6 wells at all time-points.
Subtract the autofluorescence signal from the co-cultures.
Fit a modified logistic equation to each trajectory using least squares fitting in software.
Extract parameters from the fitted trajectories.
Look for correlations between GFP and mCherry trajectory parameters.
